optionReasons.saa-med-283:option:0: Transfer Acceleration is to UPLOADS to S3 — does not reduce the cost of DISTRIBUTION of CloudFront.
optionReasons.saa-med-283:option:2: Increase TTL reduces requests to ORIGEM — the dominant cost here is the transfer of the expensive edges from Asia/Oceania, which continues.
optionReasons.saa-med-283:option:3: Signed URLs control ACESSO — bots are invented hypothesis; the cost per region continues the same.

finalJustifications: Because the Price Class 100 restricts distribution to the edges of the Americas and Europe (the cheapest): the main users keep experience and expensive regions leave the account.
Because the Price Class 100 blocks access by users in Asia and Oceania, eliminating traffic from regions that cost the bill.
Because the Price Class 100 applies a discount of 50% in all edge locations, maintaining global coverage by half of the current price.
Because the Price Class 100 moves content to cheaper regional newsletters, serving Asia directly from S3 without passing through the edges.

optionReasons.saa-med-032:option:0: The IAM is still necessary DENTRO of each account — accounts do not replace permissions.
optionReasons.saa-med-032:option:1: There is no discount per amount of accounts — Consolidated Billing aggregates usage, which is something else.
optionReasons.saa-med-032:option:2: Service limits are POR CONTA, but that's not 'folding at no cost' or the security benefit asked.

finalJustifications: Because the account is the strongest isolation frontier of the AWS: compromise or error in one does not reach the others — blast radius contained, with SCPs specific by OR.
Because separate accounts share roles IAM automatically, simplifying team access without losing isolation.
Because the separation in OUS encrypts traffic between accounts, protecting data that cross the borders of the organization.
Because each account gets an exclusive managed firewall from AWS, filtering traffic between production and development by default.

optionReasons.saa-med-174:option:0: The Trusted Advisor ALERTA then — does not prevent creation; and the requirement is blocking.
optionReasons.saa-med-174:option:1: Policies IAM in each account can be REMOVIDAS by local administrators — and configure account violates 'centralized' account'.
optionReasons.saa-med-174:option:3: The Config DETECTA and remedy after the appeal existed — does not prevent.

finalJustifications: Because the SCP in OR with condition aws:RequestedRegion denies actions outside of us-east-1/to-east-1 for TODAS the identities of the accounts — the central ceiling that the IAM location not contoured.
Because the SCP removes the extra regions from the console and APIs from the affected accounts, making them invisible to any user.
Because the SCP automatically transfers existing resources to the regions allowed, consolidating retroactive compliance.
Because the SCP grants the basic permissions in the two regions released — without it, the accounts would have no access to any region.

optionReasons.saa-med-203:option:0: Settings + SNS is DETECTION — key accesses would have already been created.
optionReasons.saa-med-203:option:2: Permission Boundaries are applied POR entity DENTRO account — local admin may not apply them; no external ceiling.
optionReasons.saa-med-203:option:3: Deny in groups IAM of the child account can be edited/removed by the account admin himself.

finalJustifications: Because the SCP with Deny explicit in iam:CreateAccessKey is a roof EXTERNO to account: applies to all identities, including the local administrator — nothing within the account contour.
Because the SCP immediately disable existing key accesses in the OR, repealing the programmatic access already granted in the organization's daughter accounts.
Because the SCP replaces policies IAM of the daughter accounts, centralizing all permissions in the management account of the organization.
Because the SCP requires MFA to create key accesses instead of blocking, adding the second factor to the flow of local account administrators.

optionReasons.saa-med-248:option:0: Lambda Iteration 50 update-stack accounts is to reimplement the StackSets in hand — fragile and without competition control/rollback.
optionReasons.saa-med-248:option:1: 'Parameter Store Override' is not a StackSets feature.
optionReasons.saa-med-248:option:2: Conformity Packs assess CONFORMIDADE — do not implement the template infrastructure.

finalJustifications: Because the StackSets with Auto Deployment (service-managed, integrated with Organizations) creates instances in new OU accounts, removes those that come out and spreads template updates to all — with competition control.
Because Auto Deployment executes the template only in the organization's management account, which transfers the resources created to the daughter accounts via sharing RAM.
Because Auto Deployment converts the template of CloudFormation in one SCP applied to the OU accounts, imposing the setting of CloudTrail as a policy rather than a resource.
Because Auto Deployment opens a manual application for approval in each child account before applying the template, guaranteeing the consent of local administrators.

optionReasons.saa-med-041:option:0: Manually restarting every day is bracal operation — not architecture solution.
optionReasons.saa-med-041:option:1: The grace period only ADIA the health assessment after the launch — does not do the ASG see application failure.
optionReasons.saa-med-041:option:2: Switch to NLB does not change the type of health check that the ASG use.

finalJustifications: Because with health check type ELB o ASG adopts the vision of the balancer (which tests the RESPOSTA HTTP): app locked = failed no ALB = replaced instance — what the status check of EC2 does not detect.
Because the health check ELB restarts the application process within the closed instance, restoring the response HTTP without having to replace the whole machine.
Because the health check ELB check the application logs for errors 5xx, detecting blockage by the exception pattern before users notice.
Because the health check ELB migrates the active connections to another instance before replacing the lock, ensuring the exchange without any lost request.

optionReasons.saa-med-042:option:1: Spot for CONTINUANCE is bet: in the failure of an AZ the capacity Spot may be disputed and disappear as well.
optionReasons.saa-med-042:option:2: ClimbING ONLY AFTER failure depends on emergency launches — when everyone disputes capacity in the region.
optionReasons.saa-med-042:option:3: Focusing everything on a 'reliable' AZ creates the single point of maximum failure.

finalJustifications: Because static resilience = provide N+1 by AZ: losing an area, the remnants still add up 100% of peak — not dependent on emergency scale-out.
Because the N+1 folds the capacity of each AZ automatically at peaks, absorbing the extra load without previous provisioning.
Because the N+1 ensures that the AWS prioritizes the account in the dispute by capacity, booking instances in surviving AZs.
Because the N+1 allows you to turn off health checks from healthy AZs, saving checks during emergency.

optionReasons.saa-med-051:option:0: Early morning Deployment only hides downtime — and rollback is still slow.
optionReasons.saa-med-051:option:1: It is the closest because it is also a named implementation strategy, of the same vocabulary — but it is the opposite end of the objective: to update all instances at the same time maximizes downtime and locks rollback; blue/green keeps the old environment ready for immediate reversal.
optionReasons.saa-med-051:option:2: Disable health checks blind balancer — users discover the bug.

finalJustifications: Because in blue/green the new environment goes up in parallel, the traffic migrates after validation and the old one is ready: problem = redirection back in seconds, downtime zero.
Because the blue/green updates half of the instances at a time, keeping the other half serving while the first one receives the version.
Because the blue/green backups the entire bank before each deployment, and the rollback restores the data along with the old code.
Because the blue/green calendars the switch to the lowest traffic schedule, reducing the impact of downtime to a few connected users.
